title: There’s something so special about getting to see a brand-new musical...
transcript: I have fallen in love with a new puppet. Her name is Princess, and she is the star of a new musical called The Snow Goose. Yes, she's the titular Snow Goose at Goodspeed Opera House. Goodspeed is one of my favourite theatres in the entire world. Genuinely, I think it is so beautiful and I will take any excuse to go see a show there. And when that excuse is a brand new musical from Scott Gilmour and Claire McKenzie, obviously I am there. Their last musical, Kaylee, was one of my top shows of 2025, so I was really excited to see this. But I didn't know anything about the source material. I'd never heard the story before, and I was unprepared for how invested I would become in a Goose. The Snow Goose follows Frith, a young girl living on the coast of England in the 1930s, and Philip, a disabled artist who lives in a lighthouse and has been cast out by the town for no reason other than the fact that he doesn't look like them. And their lives become intertwined when Frith finds an injury Snow Goose, who they named Princess, and they nurse her back to health together. Princess is brought to life through incredible puppetry. She flies, she's funny. She made me cry. And this entire cast does such remarkable work just building this coastal community where you feel invested and tender and also sometimes horrified by their choices. One of my Favorite things about the show is the disability representation. The actor who plays Philip, Eric Graves, is a double amputee. And what this story shows us is the only thing that really limits Philip is the way the world perceives him. And when Frith appears, wanting to learn from him, showing him so much respect and care, it changes the way he perceives himself. And I think that's so much of what this musical is about. Learning to trust yourself, realizing that your life is your life, and your choices are your choices. It's tender and beautiful and earnest, and the music is gorgeous. A truly stunning folk inspired score. And yes, there is this very, very good bird at its center. The Snow Goose is playing at Goodspeed Opera House through October 18th. So you have a few more weeks to fall in love with my favorite bird for yourself.
classificationReason: Creator attended The Snow Goose at Goodspeed Opera House and offers detailed first-person opinions on the puppetry, cast, and source material. Matches the regional listing.
